title: Family buyer worried 900 sqft is too small
buyer_primary_need: Assess whether the 900 sq.ft. Type A layout can fit a family of four’s usual furniture without cramped bedrooms or circulation.
key_information_learned: The household is four people, including two children.
They are concerned about fitting a sofa, dining table, and children’s beds while preserving comfortable walkways.
They understand area figures alone cannot show furniture fit and want to judge the actual layout flow.
They agreed a show-unit viewing would help and asked about available days and times; they may bring the children.
important_information_missed: The agent did not mention the retrieved project-material description that the layout has no long internal corridor, which was relevant to the circulation concern.
Exact room dimensions and a furniture-fit overlay were not available in retrieved Pearlmont Knowledge; the agent did not seek support for those details.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 900 sqft for a family sounds quite small leh.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair concern—900 sqft can feel different depending on the family’s needs. The layout has 3 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, and the project materials describe all three bedrooms as able to fit a queen bed. I wouldn’t want to assume it suits every family, though. How many people would be living there, and would you need a room for anything specific like a study or guests?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Four of us, two kids. Main worry is whether the bedrooms and living area can fit our usual furniture without making the walkway feel cramped—what are the room sizes like?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: The approximate room areas are: master bedroom 143.4 sq ft, Bedroom 1 117.4 sq ft, and Bedroom 2 103.3 sq ft. The combined living, dining and kitchen area is about 404.7 sq ft. These are area figures, not wall-to-wall dimensions, so they can’t confirm exactly how your furniture will fit or how the walkways will feel. Which piece are you most concerned about fitting—your sofa, dining table, or the kids’ beds?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Probably our sofa and dining table, plus the kids’ beds. Just worried once everything’s in, the walkway from the entrance through the living area will feel tight. Is there a foyer or is it straight into the living/dining space?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Yes—the layout has a separate foyer of about 25.9 sq ft, intended to give some privacy rather than opening directly into the living/dining area. The living, dining and kitchen area is about 404.7 sq ft. Those figures don’t confirm how much clear walkway you’d have once furnished, though. Do you know roughly how long your sofa and dining table are?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Not sure of the exact measurements, just a normal 3-seater sofa and 4-person dining table, plus single beds for the kids. The room sizes help, but hard to picture the walkway from area figures alone. Would probably need to see the actual layout or show unit to judge the flow properly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: That makes sense—walkway flow is much easier to judge in person than from area figures. The show unit should give you a better feel for the living and dining space; would you like me to help arrange a viewing?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Yeah, would be helpful to see the show unit and judge the flow. What days and times are available? We may bring the kids along too.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: I’ll get the available viewing times checked for you and mention that you may be bringing the kids along.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay thanks, please let me know what days and times are available. We’ll see if we can bring the kids along too.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: I can’t verify available viewing days or times, or whether the kids can be accommodated, because the appointment calendar isn’t connected. No booking is confirmed.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Ah okay, thanks for clarifying. If you’re able to get confirmed viewing slots later, please send them over and we’ll check what works for the family. Nothing booked for now ya.

The mock furniture check fits a 1.5m by 2.0m queen bed, with about 0.75m clear on one side and 0.65m at the foot before wardrobe placement; a full-depth wardrobe opposite the bed would make circulation tight. The plan also shows no long internal corridor. Treat these measurements as this scenario fixture only; viewing the show unit is the practical way to judge the family layout.
